q: The Rail Coach Factory is located at:

options.A: Perambur
options.B: Varanasi
options.C: Bengaluru
options.D: Kapurthala

e: The Rail Coach Factory is located at Kapurthala in Punjab.

q: Banaras Locomotive Works (BLW), Varanasi, is a production unit engaged primarily in the manufacture of:

options.A: Coaches and wagons
options.B: Locomotives
options.C: Wheels and axles
options.D: Signalling equipment

e: Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi is a production unit engaged primarily in the manufacture of locomotives.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manufacture/procurement of new rolling stock under the Rolling Stock Programme is charged to Capital (or the Depreciation Reserve Fund for replacements).
2. Periodic Overhaul of existing rolling stock is a revenue activity charged to working expenses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: new rolling stock under the Rolling Stock Programme is charged to Capital, or to the Depreciation Reserve Fund for replacements, while Periodic Overhaul of existing stock is a revenue activity charged to working expenses.

q: Which of the following is a function of the Workshop Accounts Office?

options.A: Fixing the allowed times for jobs
options.B: Operating the machines in the shops
options.C: Purchasing stores for the workshop
options.D: Internal check of labour pay sheets and stores issues and compilation of the cost of jobs

e: The Workshop Accounts Office carries out internal check of labour pay sheets and stores issues and compiles the cost of jobs; fixing allowed times, operating machines and purchasing stores are executive functions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On the executive side, a railway workshop is headed by the Chief Workshop Manager.
2. A production unit of Indian Railways is headed by a General Manager.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: on the executive side a railway workshop is headed by the Chief Workshop Manager, while a production unit of Indian Railways is headed by a General Manager.

q: An estimate prepared for a workshop manufacture job provides for:

options.A: Labour, material and on-cost required for the job
options.B: Material cost only
options.C: Labour cost only
options.D: On-cost only

e: An estimate prepared for a workshop manufacture job provides for all the elements of its cost - labour, material and on-cost required for the job.

q: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Budget, the head 'Issues to Revenue' represents:

options.A: Stores purchased for revenue works
options.B: The anticipated transfer, during the year, of outturn (repairs and manufacture) chargeable to revenue heads
options.C: The earnings of the workshop from passengers
options.D: The fines recovered from workshop staff

e: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Budget, 'Issues to Revenue' represents the anticipated transfer, during the year, of outturn - repairs and manufacture - chargeable to revenue heads.

q: Petty contingent expenses of a workshop are met from:

options.A: The personal funds of the shop incharge
options.B: The Staff Benefit Fund
options.C: The Pension Fund
options.D: A cash imprest held for the purpose, which is recouped periodically

e: Petty contingent expenses of a workshop are met from a cash imprest held for the purpose, which is recouped periodically.

q: A system of wage payment under which a worker's earnings vary directly with the output produced by him is known as:

options.A: Payment by results
options.B: Time rate system
options.C: Dearness allowance system
options.D: Subsistence allowance system

e: Under payment by results, a worker's earnings vary directly with the output produced by him, unlike the time-rate system where wages depend on time attended.

q: Ordinary repairs to a shop's machinery, when got executed through an outside agency instead of departmentally, are charged to:

options.A: Capital, because an outside agency is involved
options.B: The Pension Fund
options.C: The shop on-cost of the shop owning the machine
options.D: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as a manufacture job

e: Ordinary repairs to a shop's machinery got executed through an outside agency remain a revenue item and are charged to the shop on-cost of the shop owning the machine; use of an outside agency does not make them capital.

q: Corrective maintenance of an asset refers to the maintenance or repair work which is carried out:

options.A: At predetermined intervals, before any failure occurs
options.B: After the asset has broken down or failed, in order to restore it to working condition
options.C: Only at the time of manufacture of the asset
options.D: Only during the annual shutdown of the workshop

e: Corrective maintenance is the repair work carried out after an asset has broken down or failed, in order to restore it to working condition, as distinct from preventive maintenance done before failure.

q:
Consider the following statements about preventive maintenance:
1. It is planned maintenance carried out at scheduled intervals, before a failure occurs.
2. By checking failures in advance, it reduces the incidence of breakdowns and the need for corrective repairs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: preventive maintenance is planned maintenance carried out at scheduled intervals before a failure occurs, and by checking failures in advance it reduces breakdowns and the need for corrective repairs.

q: The provisions governing the working and accounts of railway workshops are contained in:

options.A: The Indian Railway Code for the Rolling Stock Department (Rolling Stock Code)
options.B: The Indian Railway Stores Code
options.C: The Indian Railway Traffic (Commercial) Code
options.D: The General Financial Rules

e: The provisions governing the working and accounts of railway workshops are contained in the Indian Railway Code for the Rolling Stock Department, known as the Rolling Stock Code.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 'codal life' of rolling stock is the prescribed economic service life of the stock, on the completion of which it normally becomes due for condemnation and replacement.
2. Rolling stock which has completed its codal life is automatically condemned, without any examination of its condition.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: codal life is the prescribed economic service life on completion of which stock normally becomes due for condemnation and replacement, but condemnation is not automatic - it follows examination of the stock's condition.

q: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Budget, the head 'Issues to Capital' represents:

options.A: The cash paid for purchase of new machinery for the workshop
options.B: The fines and penalties recovered from workshop staff
options.C: Stores purchased directly for capital works
options.D: The anticipated outturn of manufacture and repair work to be transferred to Capital heads during the year

e: In the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Budget, 'Issues to Capital' represents the anticipated outturn of manufacture and repair work to be transferred to Capital heads during the year.

q: Material or finished articles are allowed to be taken out of a railway workshop premises only:

options.A: On the verbal permission of the chargeman
options.B: Under a gate pass issued by the competent authority
options.C: Against a personal surety of the worker carrying them
options.D: After the close of the financial year

e: Material or finished articles are allowed to be taken out of the workshop premises only under a gate pass issued by the competent authority.

q: The millwright shop of a workshop is primarily responsible for:

options.A: The manufacture of patterns for the foundry
options.B: The upholstery and trimming of coaches
options.C: The installation, maintenance and repair of the machinery and plant of the workshop
options.D: The painting of coaches and wagons

e: The millwright shop is primarily responsible for the installation, maintenance and repair of the machinery and plant of the workshop.

q: In a workshop, the turning of wheel tyres to profile and the mounting/pressing of wheels on axles is carried out in:

options.A: The erecting shop
options.B: The smithy
options.C: The paint shop
options.D: The wheel shop

e: The turning of wheel tyres to profile and the mounting and pressing of wheels on axles is carried out in the wheel shop.

q: Where a job in progress in a workshop is abandoned midway, the expenditure accumulated on it under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:

options.A: Adjusted under the orders of the competent authority, and is not allowed to remain indefinitely under the suspense head
options.B: Automatically transferred to the Pension Fund
options.C: Recovered from the wages of the workers who worked on the job
options.D: Carried forward unchanged from year to year without any orders

e: Where a job is abandoned midway, the expenditure accumulated on it under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is adjusted under the orders of the competent authority and is not allowed to remain indefinitely under the suspense head.

q: Scrap arising in a shop which cannot be identified with any particular job is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting its value to the last job completed in the shop
options.B: Crediting its value to shop on-cost
options.C: Debiting its value to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: Treating it as a personal perquisite of the shop incharge

e: Scrap arising in a shop which cannot be identified with any particular job is credited to shop on-cost, so that it reduces the overheads spread over the jobs of the shop.

q: Overtime work in a workshop is undertaken:

options.A: Whenever the chargeman considers it necessary, without any sanction
options.B: Only on days when the workshop remains closed
options.C: Only by casual labour engaged for the purpose
options.D: Only with the prior sanction of the competent authority

e: Overtime work in a workshop is undertaken only with the prior sanction of the competent authority; it cannot be ordered merely at the chargeman's discretion.

q:
Consider the following statements about the allowances included in the allowed time for a job:
1. Relaxation (fatigue) allowance is provided to enable the worker to recover from fatigue and to attend to personal needs.
2. Contingency allowance is provided to cover small unavoidable delays inherent in the job, which cannot be eliminated.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: relaxation (fatigue) allowance enables the worker to recover from fatigue and attend to personal needs, and contingency allowance covers small unavoidable delays inherent in the job which cannot be eliminated.

q: The cost of protective clothing and safety equipment supplied to shop staff for use on their work is charged to:

options.A: Shop on-cost
options.B: The individual jobs on which the staff happen to be working
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: The personal accounts of the staff concerned

e: The cost of protective clothing and safety equipment supplied to shop staff for use on their work is charged to shop on-cost.

q: Routine Overhaul (ROH) of wagons, as distinct from their Periodic Overhaul, is carried out:

options.A: Only in production units
options.B: Only at the Railway Board's workshops
options.C: In wagon depots (sick lines), and not in workshops
options.D: At the stations where the wagons are loaded

e: Routine Overhaul of wagons, as distinct from their Periodic Overhaul, is carried out in wagon depots (sick lines), and not in workshops.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of normal idle time of workers is treated as production overhead and charged to on-cost.
2. The cost of abnormal idle time, such as that caused by a prolonged strike or a major breakdown, is also absorbed in the cost of jobs in the same way as normal idle time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: the cost of normal idle time is production overhead charged to on-cost, whereas abnormal idle time, such as that caused by a prolonged strike or major breakdown, is not absorbed in job costs in the same way.

q: The Productivity Linked Bonus paid to railway employees differs from the incentive bonus in a workshop in that the Productivity Linked Bonus:

options.A: Is earned only by the workers of one particular shop
options.B: Is computed on the time saved by each individual worker
options.C: Is paid only in production units manufacturing locomotives
options.D: Is a railway-wide payment linked to the productivity of the Railways as a whole, and not to the outturn of an individual worker or shop

e: The Productivity Linked Bonus is a railway-wide payment linked to the productivity of the Railways as a whole, whereas workshop incentive bonus depends on the outturn or time saved of the individual worker or shop.

q:
Consider the following statements about work study:
1. Work study comprises method study and work measurement.
2. Work measurement is concerned with determining the time required for a qualified worker to carry out a specified job at a defined rate of working.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: work study comprises method study and work measurement, and work measurement is concerned with determining the time required for a qualified worker to carry out a specified job at a defined rate of working.

q: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW) is a production unit engaged primarily in the manufacture of:

options.A: Passenger coaches
options.B: Electric locomotives
options.C: Wheels and axles
options.D: Diesel locomotives only

e: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is a production unit engaged primarily in the manufacture of electric locomotives.

q: The Modern Coach Factory, which manufactures passenger coaches, is located at:

options.A: Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh
options.B: Kapurthala, Punjab
options.C: Perambur, Chennai
options.D: Yelahanka, Bengaluru

e: The Modern Coach Factory, which manufactures passenger coaches, is located at Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Diesel Loco Modernisation Works, engaged in the rebuilding/modernisation of diesel locomotives and manufacture of their components, is located at:

options.A: Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
options.B: Jamalpur, Bihar
options.C: Patiala, Punjab
options.D: Golden Rock, Tiruchirappalli

e: The Diesel Loco Modernisation Works, engaged in the rebuilding and modernisation of diesel locomotives and manufacture of their components, is located at Patiala, Punjab.

q: Railway workshops are 'factories' within the meaning of:

options.A: The Indian Railways Act, 1989
options.B: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
options.C: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
options.D: The Factories Act, 1948

e: Railway workshops are 'factories' within the meaning of the Factories Act, 1948, so its provisions on working hours, safety and welfare apply to them.

q: The Workshop General Register, in which the cost of jobs is compiled work order-wise, is maintained in:

options.A: The stores depot attached to the workshop
options.B: The Workshop Accounts Office
options.C: The Production Control Organisation
options.D: The office of the Chief Workshop Manager

e: The Workshop General Register, in which the cost of jobs is compiled work order-wise, is maintained in the Workshop Accounts Office.

q: On the accounts side, the Workshop Accounts Officer of a workshop functions under:

options.A: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the zonal railway
options.B: The Controller of Stores of the zonal railway
options.C: The Chief Workshop Manager of the workshop
options.D: The Railway Audit office

e: On the accounts side, the Workshop Accounts Officer of a workshop functions under the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the zonal railway.

q: The Account Current rendered by a workshop accounts office is:

options.A: A statement of the cash balance held in the workshop imprest
options.B: A list of the jobs remaining incomplete at the end of the year
options.C: A periodical (monthly) statement of the transfer transactions between the workshop accounting unit and other accounting units
options.D: A statement of the stores issued to jobs during the day

e: The Account Current rendered by a workshop accounts office is a periodical (monthly) statement of the transfer transactions between the workshop accounting unit and other accounting units.

q: In a process shop of a workshop, the cost of production is compiled by:

options.A: Accumulating the cost separately for every individual article produced
options.B: Charging the entire cost of the shop to a single work order for the year
options.C: Debiting the cost to the stores price ledger
options.D: Accumulating the cost process-wise for a period, the unit cost being arrived at by dividing the process cost by the output of the period

e: In a process shop, the cost of production is accumulated process-wise for a period, and the unit cost is arrived at by dividing the process cost by the output of the period.

q: Separate on-cost rates worked out for each shop give more accurate job costs than a single blanket rate for the whole workshop because:

options.A: A blanket rate is prohibited under the Rolling Stock Code
options.B: The indirect expenses of different shops differ widely, and a blanket rate would overcharge some jobs and undercharge others
options.C: Shops are not permitted to have their own on-cost accounts
options.D: A blanket rate can be applied only to capital jobs

e: Separate on-cost rates for each shop give more accurate job costs because the indirect expenses of different shops differ widely; a single blanket rate would overcharge some jobs and undercharge others.

q: Under an incentive (premium bonus) scheme, the benefit of the time saved on a job is shared in that:

options.A: The worker receives a bonus for the time saved, while the labour cost per unit of outturn to the Railway also falls
options.B: The entire value of the time saved is paid to the worker as bonus
options.C: The entire value of the time saved is retained by the Railway and the worker gets nothing extra
options.D: The value of the time saved is credited to the Staff Benefit Fund

e: Under an incentive (premium bonus) scheme, the benefit of time saved is shared: the worker receives a bonus for the time saved, while the labour cost per unit of outturn to the Railway also falls.

q: In foundry costing, the 'yield' of the foundry is expressed as:

options.A: The weight of metal charged into the cupola per worker
options.B: The number of moulds prepared per day
options.C: The weight of good castings obtained, expressed as a proportion (percentage) of the total metallic charge melted
options.D: The weight of coke consumed per tonne of castings

e: In foundry costing, 'yield' is the weight of good castings obtained, expressed as a proportion (percentage) of the total metallic charge melted.

q: The machinery and plant recorded in the Plant Register of a workshop are:

options.A: Never verified after their initial installation
options.B: Verified only when the Workshop Accounts Officer is transferred
options.C: Sold and replaced every year
options.D: Physically verified periodically, and shortages or discrepancies noticed are investigated and adjusted under competent orders

e: Machinery and plant in the Plant Register are physically verified periodically, and shortages or discrepancies noticed are investigated and adjusted under competent orders.

q: The buildings and plant of a railway workshop are generally not insured with commercial insurers because:

options.A: Insurance of government property is prohibited by the Factories Act
options.B: The Government, as a matter of policy, bears its own risks and does not insure its property
options.C: Workshop assets have no insurable value
options.D: The premium is charged to shop on-cost, which the shops refuse to bear

e: The buildings and plant of a railway workshop are generally not insured with commercial insurers because the Government, as a matter of policy, bears its own risks and does not insure its property.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where designs and drawings are prepared exclusively for a particular job, their cost is charged to that job.
2. The entire expenses of the drawing office of a workshop are charged to the first job designed during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: where designs and drawings are prepared exclusively for a particular job, their cost is charged to that job; the entire expenses of the drawing office are never loaded on the first job designed in the year.

q: The incentive bonus payable to workshop staff for a period is:

options.A: Computed by the stores depot on the basis of material issued
options.B: Paid at a flat rate to all staff, irrespective of outturn
options.C: Computed by the executive on the basis of the outturn and the allowed times, and checked by the Workshop Accounts Office before payment
options.D: Computed by the Railway Audit office after the annual accounts are closed

e: The incentive bonus for a period is computed by the executive on the basis of the outturn and the allowed times, and is checked by the Workshop Accounts Office before payment.

q: The period for which a rolling stock unit remains detained in a workshop for its overhaul is watched closely because:

options.A: Detention earns incentive bonus for the shop staff
options.B: The unit is charged rent by the workshop for every day of detention
options.C: Detained stock is transferred to the stores depot after one month
options.D: Prolonged detention reduces the effective availability of rolling stock for traffic

e: The detention of a rolling stock unit in the workshop is watched closely because prolonged detention reduces the effective availability of rolling stock for traffic.

q: Before the job cards/tally sheets of a shop are rendered to the Accounts office, the time booked by the workers is certified by:

options.A: The stores depot
options.B: The shop supervision (chargeman/foreman) of the shop concerned
options.C: The Production Control Organisation
options.D: The cash office of the workshop

e: Before the job cards and tally sheets are rendered to the Accounts office, the time booked by the workers is certified by the shop supervision, that is, the chargeman or foreman of the shop concerned.

q: Under the Halsey-Weir premium bonus plan, the bonus payable to a worker is generally:

options.A: 30 per cent of the value of the time saved by him
options.B: 50 per cent of the value of the time saved by him
options.C: 75 per cent of the value of the time saved by him
options.D: Equal to the full value of the time saved by him

e: Under the Halsey-Weir premium bonus plan, the bonus payable to a worker is generally 30 per cent of the value of the time saved by him.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the straight piece-rate system, a worker's earnings depend only on the output produced by him, and no time wage is guaranteed.
2. Under premium bonus plans such as the Halsey and Rowan plans, the time wages of the worker are guaranteed and a bonus is paid for the time saved.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: under the straight piece-rate system earnings depend only on output and no time wage is guaranteed, while under premium bonus plans like Halsey and Rowan the time wages are guaranteed and a bonus is paid for time saved.

q: The time-rate system of wage payment is most suitable for work:

options.A: Which is highly repetitive and easily measurable
options.B: Which cannot be measured accurately, or where quality and precision are more important than the quantity of output
options.C: Done exclusively under the Group Incentive Scheme
options.D: Done only by casual labour

e: The time-rate system is most suitable for work which cannot be measured accurately, or where quality and precision are more important than the quantity of output.

q: A system of payment by results is most suitable where:

options.A: The work is of a purely supervisory nature
options.B: The output of each worker cannot be identified
options.C: Quality considerations entirely override the quantity of output
options.D: The work is standardised and repetitive and the output of the workers can be measured accurately

e: A system of payment by results is most suitable where the work is standardised and repetitive and the output of the workers can be measured accurately.

q: Work sampling is commonly used in a workshop to determine:

options.A: The proportion of time spent by men and machines on various activities, including the extent of idleness
options.B: The chemical composition of metals used on jobs
options.C: The price of stores items in the price ledger
options.D: The periodicity of overhaul of rolling stock

e: Work sampling is commonly used to determine the proportion of time spent by men and machines on various activities, including the extent of idleness.

q: In work measurement, the predetermined motion time system known as MTM stands for:

options.A: Machine Time Measurement
options.B: Material Transfer Method
options.C: Methods-Time Measurement
options.D: Measured Task Method

e: In work measurement, the predetermined motion time system MTM stands for Methods-Time Measurement.

q: Apprentices engaged in a railway workshop under the Apprentices Act, 1961 are:

options.A: Regular employees of the workshop on time-scale pay
options.B: Trainees, who are paid a stipend during their training and are not treated as workers/employees of the workshop
options.C: Casual labour engaged on daily wages
options.D: Paid bonus under the incentive scheme like other workers

e: Apprentices engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961 are trainees who are paid a stipend during their training; they are not treated as workers or employees of the workshop.

q: The primary maintenance of a coaching train, i.e., its complete examination and attention before it commences its next trip, is carried out:

options.A: In the workshop where the coaches were manufactured
options.B: At every station where the train halts
options.C: Only during the Periodic Overhaul of the coaches
options.D: At the base (home) coaching depot to which the train belongs

e: The primary maintenance of a coaching train, that is, its complete examination and attention before it commences its next trip, is carried out at the base (home) coaching depot to which the train belongs.

q: The cost of internal transport of material within a workshop, such as the working of cranes and traversers serving the workshop as a whole, is treated as:

options.A: General on-cost of the workshop
options.B: A direct charge on the job for which material was last moved
options.C: A charge to the Capital head of the workshop
options.D: A deduction from the material cost of jobs

e: The cost of internal transport of material within a workshop, such as the working of cranes and traversers serving the workshop as a whole, is treated as general on-cost of the workshop.

q: Freight and carriage paid on material purchased specially for a particular job is:

options.A: Charged to general on-cost of the workshop
options.B: Charged to the stores depot as its handling expense
options.C: Recovered from the supplier in all cases
options.D: Charged to that job as a direct expense, forming part of its prime cost

e: Freight and carriage paid on material purchased specially for a particular job is charged to that job as a direct expense, forming part of its prime cost.

q: The maintenance of the machinery and plant of a workshop itself is carried out:

options.A: Only when a machine breaks down completely
options.B: In accordance with planned maintenance schedules, in addition to repairs of breakdowns as they occur
options.C: Only by the manufacturers of the machines
options.D: Only at the time of the annual accounts closing

e: The maintenance of the machinery and plant of a workshop itself is carried out in accordance with planned maintenance schedules, in addition to repairs of breakdowns as they occur.

q: Under Taylor's differential piece-rate system, a worker is paid:

options.A: Time wages plus 50 per cent of the value of the time saved by him
options.B: At a higher piece rate if he attains or exceeds the standard output, and at a lower piece rate if he falls short of it
options.C: A bonus equal to (time saved / time allowed) x time taken x hourly rate
options.D: A guaranteed time wage having no relation to his output

e: Under Taylor's differential piece-rate system, a worker is paid at a higher piece rate if he attains or exceeds the standard output, and at a lower piece rate if he falls short of it.

q: Method study, as a part of work study, is undertaken primarily to:

options.A: Fix the wages payable to workshop staff
options.B: Determine the bonus earned by a gang of workers
options.C: Examine and improve the method of doing the work, so that time is thereafter measured for the standardised method
options.D: Distribute the on-cost of a shop over its jobs

e: Method study, as a part of work study, is undertaken to examine and improve the method of doing the work, so that time is thereafter measured for the standardised method.

q: In work measurement, a worker working at the standard (normal) pace is assigned a rating of:
e: In work measurement, a worker working at the standard (normal) pace is assigned a rating of 100.

q: Where one worker attends to several machines, the allowance added in fixing the allowed time to cover the waiting of machines for the operator's attention is known as:

options.A: Fatigue allowance
options.B: Contingency allowance
options.C: Policy allowance
options.D: Interference allowance

e: Where one worker attends to several machines, the allowance added in the allowed time to cover the waiting of machines for the operator's attention is known as the interference allowance.

q: For a batch of components produced on a machine, the machine setting-up time is taken into account in the allowed time by:

options.A: Charging it wholly to the first piece of the batch
options.B: Spreading it over the whole batch, i.e., adding the setting-up time divided by the batch quantity to the per-piece time
options.C: Ignoring it altogether, as it is not productive time
options.D: Treating it as idle time of the operator

e: For a batch of components, the machine setting-up time is spread over the whole batch, that is, the setting-up time divided by the batch quantity is added to the per-piece allowed time.

q: Which of the following categories of workshop staff are NOT covered under the incentive scheme?

options.A: Direct workers engaged on measured jobs
options.B: Essential indirect workers attached to the shops
options.C: General indirect and office (clerical) staff not connected with production
options.D: Gang workers sharing the bonus of their group

e: General indirect and office (clerical) staff not connected with production are not covered under the incentive scheme; direct workers, essential indirect workers and gang workers are covered.

q: The paint shop of a railway workshop is primarily concerned with:

options.A: Painting, varnishing and finishing/lining of coaches, wagons and components
options.B: Manufacture of paint from raw materials
options.C: Overhaul of bogies of coaches and wagons
options.D: Melting of metals for castings

e: The paint shop of a railway workshop is primarily concerned with the painting, varnishing and finishing or lining of coaches, wagons and components.

q: The smithy of a railway workshop carries out principally:

options.A: Wood work for coach bodies
options.B: Upholstery and trimming work
options.C: Casting of components in moulds
options.D: Forging work, i.e., shaping heated metal for the manufacture and repair of components

e: The smithy principally carries out forging work, that is, shaping heated metal for the manufacture and repair of components.

q: Wood-working and coach-body timber work in a railway workshop is carried out in the:

options.A: Smithy
options.B: Carpentry (wood-working) shop
options.C: Foundry
options.D: Wheel shop

e: Wood-working and coach-body timber work in a railway workshop is carried out in the carpentry (wood-working) shop.

q: Repairs to the electrical equipment of coaches, such as fans, lights and dynamos/batteries, are carried out in a workshop in the:

options.A: Paint shop
options.B: Millwright shop
options.C: Electrical shop
options.D: Tool room

e: Repairs to the electrical equipment of coaches, such as fans, lights and dynamos or batteries, are carried out in the electrical shop.

q: The manufacture and repair of laminated and coil springs for rolling stock in a workshop is done in the:

options.A: Spring shop
options.B: Erecting shop
options.C: Paint shop
options.D: Pattern shop

e: The manufacture and repair of laminated and coil springs for rolling stock is done in the spring shop.

q: Overhaul and repair of the bogies of coaches and wagons in a workshop is carried out in the:

options.A: Foundry
options.B: Smithy
options.C: Upholstery shop
options.D: Bogie shop

e: Overhaul and repair of the bogies of coaches and wagons is carried out in the bogie shop.

q: In a carriage and wagon depot, the 'sick line' refers to:

options.A: The line on which trains are washed and cleaned
options.B: The lines where stock requiring repairs or attention is placed and dealt with
options.C: The line reserved for accident relief trains
options.D: The rest room provided for sick staff of the depot

e: In a carriage and wagon depot, the 'sick line' refers to the lines where stock requiring repairs or attention is placed and dealt with.

q: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela (Bihar) is a production unit engaged in the manufacture of:

options.A: Locomotives
options.B: Passenger coaches
options.C: Wheels for rolling stock
options.D: Rails and sleepers

e: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela, Bihar, is a production unit engaged in the manufacture of wheels for rolling stock.

q: The Rail Spring Karkhana at Sithouli (near Gwalior) manufactures:

options.A: Springs for rolling stock
options.B: Wheels and axles
options.C: Electric locomotives
options.D: Signalling cables

e: The Rail Spring Karkhana at Sithouli, near Gwalior, manufactures springs for rolling stock.

q: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop is located at:

options.A: Jamalpur
options.B: Kharagpur
options.C: Matunga, Mumbai
options.D: Tiruchirappalli

e: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop is located at Tiruchirappalli.

q: The Jamalpur Workshop of Eastern Railway is situated in the State of:

options.A: West Bengal
options.B: Bihar
options.C: Jharkhand
options.D: Uttar Pradesh

e: The Jamalpur Workshop of Eastern Railway is situated in the State of Bihar.

q: A workshop employee who has to go out of the workshop premises during working hours must:

options.A: Obtain a gate pass or the permission of the competent authority
options.B: Merely inform a co-worker in his shop
options.C: Surrender his job card permanently at the gate
options.D: Wait until the close of the financial year

e: A workshop employee who has to go out of the workshop premises during working hours must obtain a gate pass or the permission of the competent authority.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker in a workshop (factory) cannot ordinarily be required or allowed to work for more than:

options.A: 60 hours in a week
options.B: 48 hours in a week
options.C: 36 hours in a week
options.D: 72 hours in a week

e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker in a factory cannot ordinarily be required or allowed to work for more than 48 hours in a week.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a canteen facility for the workers is required to be provided in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed exceeds:
e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a canteen facility is required to be provided in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed exceeds 250.

q: Which of the following is NOT charged as an element of the cost of a workshop job?

options.A: Interest on the capital invested in the workshop
options.B: Direct material consumed on the job
options.C: Proforma on-cost, i.e., Provident Fund contribution and depreciation
options.D: Shop on-cost and general on-cost

e: Interest on the capital invested in the workshop is not charged as an element of the cost of a job; direct material, proforma on-cost and shop and general on-cost are charged.

q: Which of the following is NOT a direct charge on a workshop job?

options.A: The cost of a pattern made specially for that job
options.B: Freight paid on material purchased specially for that job
options.C: Hire charges of special equipment engaged exclusively for that job
options.D: The cost of the Chief Workshop Manager's office establishment, which is borne as general on-cost

e: The cost of the Chief Workshop Manager's office establishment is not a direct charge on a job, since it is borne as general on-cost; job-specific pattern cost, special freight and hire of special equipment are direct charges.

q: The cost of a job executed in a railway workshop does not include:

options.A: Shop on-cost
options.B: Selling and distribution expenses
options.C: Proforma on-cost
options.D: Direct labour booked on the job

e: The cost of a workshop job includes direct labour, material, shop on-cost and proforma on-cost, but it does not include selling and distribution expenses.

q: In the terminology of cost accounting, the workshop 'on-cost' corresponds broadly to:

options.A: Prime cost
options.B: Direct expenses chargeable to a job
options.C: Factory (works) overheads
options.D: Administrative overheads of the Railway Board

e: In cost accounting terminology, the workshop 'on-cost' corresponds broadly to factory (works) overheads, that is, the indirect production expenses absorbed on jobs.

q: The cost of constructing an extension to a workshop building is charged:

options.A: To Capital/Depreciation Reserve Fund through a works estimate
options.B: To Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: To shop on-cost of the shop housed in the building
options.D: To a revenue standing work order

e: The cost of constructing an extension to a workshop building is a capital work, charged to Capital or the Depreciation Reserve Fund through a works estimate.

q: A component of a specific job got fabricated through an outside agency is accounted for by:

options.A: Charging the agency's bill to shop on-cost
options.B: Charging the agency's bill to general on-cost
options.C: Ignoring the bill in the cost of the job
options.D: Charging the agency's bill to that job as a direct expense

e: A component of a specific job got fabricated through an outside agency is charged to that job as a direct expense, on the basis of the agency's bill.

q: Work executed in a railway workshop for private parties or outside bodies is:

options.A: Never permitted under any circumstances
options.B: Undertaken only with the sanction of the competent authority, its full cost together with departmental charges being recovered from the party
options.C: Executed free of charge as a public service
options.D: Charged at the cost of material only

e: Work executed in a workshop for private parties or outside bodies is undertaken only with the sanction of the competent authority, and its full cost together with departmental charges is recovered from the party.

q: Moulding sand used in the foundry of a workshop is a consumable material, and its cost is borne:

options.A: By the pattern shop as its own expense
options.B: By the stores depot as a stock loss
options.C: As part of the foundry's process/on-cost charges, spread over the castings produced
options.D: By debit to Capital

e: Moulding sand is a consumable material of the foundry, and its cost is borne as part of the foundry's process or on-cost charges, spread over the castings produced.

q: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is reflected in the Balance Sheet of the railway as:

options.A: A liability of the railway
options.B: A revenue receipt of the year
options.C: A part of the Pension Fund
options.D: An asset, representing the work-in-progress in the workshops

e: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is shown in the Balance Sheet of the railway as an asset, representing the work-in-progress in the workshops.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Depreciation Reserve Fund is fed by appropriations made from revenue (working expenses).
2. Amounts accumulated in the Depreciation Reserve Fund can be used only for the replacement of workshop machinery, and for no other asset.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: the Depreciation Reserve Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue (working expenses); but the fund is used for replacement of assets generally, not only of workshop machinery, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Before a rolling stock unit is taken up for Periodic Overhaul in a workshop, the usual first step is:

options.A: Complete dismantling of the unit
options.B: Examination of the unit and assessment of the repairs required, so that the scope of the overhaul is decided
options.C: Painting of the unit in the new livery
options.D: Transfer of the unit to the stores depot

e: Before a rolling stock unit is taken up for Periodic Overhaul, the usual first step is examination of the unit and assessment of the repairs required, so that the scope of the overhaul is decided.

q: Repairs to accident-damaged rolling stock received in a workshop are ordinarily taken up:

options.A: Only after the whole annual programme of the workshop is completed
options.B: At the end of the financial year
options.C: On priority, as emergent work, so that the stock is restored to service early
options.D: Only in production units, and never in repair workshops

e: Repairs to accident-damaged rolling stock received in a workshop are ordinarily taken up on priority, as emergent work, so that the stock is restored to service early.

q: The expenditure on testing and trial runs of a newly manufactured locomotive or coach, before its acceptance, is treated as:

options.A: A charge to the shop on-cost of the workshop as a whole
options.B: A revenue expense of the open line
options.C: A loss to be written off to revenue
options.D: A part of the cost of manufacture of that unit, charged to its job

e: The expenditure on testing and trial runs of a newly manufactured locomotive or coach, before its acceptance, is treated as part of the cost of manufacture of that unit and charged to its job.

q: For non-repetitive jobs, where continuous stop-watch study is impracticable, allowed times are fixed by:

options.A: Analytical estimating, building up the time from synthetic/standard data and the judgement of trained estimators
options.B: Asking each worker to name his own time for the job
options.C: Adopting the allowed time of an unrelated job
options.D: Dispensing with allowed times for such jobs altogether

e: For non-repetitive jobs, where continuous stop-watch study is impracticable, allowed times are fixed by analytical estimating, building up the time from synthetic or standard data and the judgement of trained estimators.

q: For components manufactured regularly in a workshop, standard costs are prescribed so that:

options.A: Actual job costs need never be compiled for such components
options.B: The actual cost of each batch or job can be compared with the standard cost and the variations analysed for cost control
options.C: No on-cost need be charged on such jobs
options.D: The components can be sold to the trade at the standard cost

e: Standard costs are prescribed for regularly manufactured components so that the actual cost of each batch or job can be compared with the standard cost and the variations analysed for cost control.

q: A characteristic feature of the Rowan premium bonus plan is that:

options.A: The bonus is always 50 per cent of the worker's time wages
options.B: The worker receives the entire value of the time saved by him
options.C: As more and more time is saved, the bonus increases at a diminishing rate, which protects the employer against loosely fixed allowed times
options.D: No time wages are guaranteed to the worker under the plan

e: Under the Rowan plan, the bonus varies with the proportion of time saved to time allowed, so as more and more time is saved the bonus increases at a diminishing rate, protecting the employer against loosely fixed allowed times.

q: An allowed time which has been fixed more liberally (longer) than the time properly required for a job is known in work measurement as:

options.A: A tight rate
options.B: A standard rate
options.C: A synthesis rate
options.D: A loose rate

e: An allowed time which has been fixed more liberally, that is, longer, than the time properly required for a job is known in work measurement as a loose rate.

q: Departmental charges levied in addition to cost on work done for other departments or outside bodies represent broadly:

options.A: A recovery towards the establishment, supervision and tools and plant expenses of the department executing the work
options.B: A profit margin retained by the Railway Board
options.C: The cost of the raw material used on the work
options.D: A penalty imposed on the indenting department

e: Departmental charges levied in addition to cost on work done for other departments or outside bodies represent broadly a recovery towards the establishment, supervision and tools and plant expenses of the executing department.

q: Under the incentive scheme, the time spent by a worker in rectifying his own defective work:

options.A: Earns bonus at double the normal rate
options.B: Earns no bonus, bonus being payable only on accepted good work
options.C: Is treated as leave without pay
options.D: Is charged to the next job taken up by him

e: Under the incentive scheme, the time spent by a worker in rectifying his own defective work earns no bonus, because bonus is payable only on accepted good work.

q: It is noticed that labour and material have been booked to a wrong work order. The correction is effected by:

options.A: Erasing the original entry in the shop records
options.B: Booking the amount again to the correct work order without any adjustment of the wrong booking
options.C: Transfer entries debiting the correct work order and crediting the wrong one, passed under proper approval
options.D: Writing off the amount to the Pension Fund

e: Booking of labour and material to a wrong work order is corrected by transfer entries debiting the correct work order and crediting the wrong one, passed under proper approval; the original entry is not erased.

q: Where castings for several jobs are poured from a common melt in the foundry, the common melting cost is apportioned among the jobs on the basis of:

options.A: The number of workers engaged in the foundry
options.B: The floor area occupied by the foundry
options.C: The number of moulding boxes used
options.D: The weight of metal poured for each job

e: Where castings for several jobs are poured from a common melt, the common melting cost is apportioned among the jobs on the basis of the weight of metal poured for each job.

q: The cost of a locomotive or coach manufactured in a production unit is compiled:

options.A: Unit-wise, for each individual unit turned out, comprising material, labour and on-cost including proforma charges
options.B: For all the units turned out in a year together, in one lump sum
options.C: At the prevailing market price of a similar unit
options.D: On the basis of material cost only, unit-wise

e: The cost of a locomotive or coach manufactured in a production unit is compiled unit-wise, for each individual unit turned out, comprising material, labour and on-cost including proforma charges.

q: A 'standard hour' in work measurement denotes:

options.A: The clock hour in which the maximum work is done in a shop
options.B: The hour of attendance recorded on the gate card
options.C: The quantity of work which a qualified worker can turn out in one hour working at standard performance
options.D: An overtime hour paid at double the normal rate

e: A 'standard hour' denotes the quantity of work which a qualified worker can turn out in one hour working at standard performance.

q: In railway accounts, the abbreviation 'T&P' stands for:

options.A: Trains and Parcels
options.B: Time and Pay
options.C: Transfer and Posting
options.D: Tools and Plant

e: In railway accounts, the abbreviation 'T&P' stands for Tools and Plant.

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the 'group' whose outturn is measured for incentive ordinarily comprises:

options.A: All the workshops of the railway taken together
options.B: The workers of a shop or section, including the essential indirect workers attached to it
options.C: Only the supervisory staff of the shop
options.D: Only the apprentices undergoing training in the shop

e: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the group whose outturn is measured ordinarily comprises the workers of a shop or section, including the essential indirect workers attached to it.
